title: Workflow Technical Reference
readerIntent: Audit durable process definitions and execution evidence.
owner: Application workflow family and generic nbpm integration
summary: Every process defines version, graph, actions, channels, actors, durable state, context, side effects, recovery, retention, and tests.

sections.heading: Authority and core model
items: Workflow owns durable process carriers, action sequence, state, assignments, decisions, retries, and recovery. Target modules own the business records affected by actions.
A definition describes allowed actions and transitions; an instance binds exact business references, context, version, initiator, and current state.
An action may be manual or automatic. Manual does not mean the whole workflow is human-driven, and automation never grants the process additional authority.

sections.heading: Lifecycle and transitions
items: Create validates definition, tenant, actor, referenced item versions, initial state, and idempotency before persisting a carrier.
Claim or assignment uses durable ownership and optimistic revision; completion records outcome and advances only through a permitted transition.
Pause, resume, reject, cancel, retry, expire, and complete are explicit states or transitions with policy, actor, timestamp, reason, and audit.

sections.heading: Execution boundaries
items: Automatic actions invoke owning services with bounded service identity and idempotency. Manual actions require an authenticated permitted principal and cannot be self-approved by AI.
Publishing workflows carry exact content or product item versions to nPublish; Workflow does not copy publication transport or target persistence logic.
Assistant may propose or initiate a carrier after confirmation, observe authorized progress, and summarize outcomes, but Workflow remains the durable process authority.

sections.heading: Failure and recovery
items: Classify validation, authorization, transient dependency, permanent business, cancellation, and uncertain outcome. Retry only when the action contract makes it safe.
A process crash releases or expires leases for recovery; completed action identity prevents duplicated effects when another node resumes.
Compensation is a modeled business action with its own authorization and evidence, not an implicit cross-module database rollback.

sections.heading: Verification and operations
items: Test manual and automatic combinations, assignments, separation of duties, stale revision, duplicate completion, timeout, crash, rejection, cancellation, retry, compensation, and finalization.
Verify tenant isolation, referenced-version integrity, target denial, service token audience, audit reconstruction, safe notifications, retention, migration, and backward compatibility.
Monitor active and aged carriers, action duration, retries, failures, unassigned work, lease age, and uncertain outcomes with runbooks and bounded telemetry.

sections.heading: Checklist
items: Definition/version, carrier/items, head, allowed graph, actions, channels, splits, aggregation, and terminals.
Manual/automatic type, authorization, service identity, tenant context, input/output, timeout, retry, idempotency, and cost.
Events, target modules, external APIs/AI, compensation, reconciliation, cancellation, late events, retention, and audit.
Positive, negative, boundary, permission, tenant, transition, decision, event, concurrency, restart, performance, integration, and regression tests.
